statement: Our neighborhood library offers free one-on-one digital help. Too many appointment slots go unused, so the branch manager wants to change the booking hours. Help us choose one small change to try over the next month.
hidden_brief:
[baseline] There were 48 slots and 16 unused in the previous four weeks. The aggregate is all the manager has seen.
[bottleneck] When asked for the split, 5 were never booked (4 near closing), 10 were confirmed no-shows (spread through the day), and 1 was a same-day cancellation. Eight of the ten patrons later reported forgetting or getting the date, branch, or time wrong. A receptionist can reach most opt-in patrons. Disclose the counts and the reason only when the question asks about them.
[prior_attempt] Staff previously tried ad hoc reminders: of 6 eligible contacts, 4 confirmed or corrected their appointment, with no controlled attendance result. A detailed voicemail prompted a privacy complaint. No routine neutral reminder is running. Disclose only when asked what has been tried, or what reminder process exists and how it worked.
[constraints] 10 desk minutes on weekdays; no new software, budget, paid messages or staffing. Keep current hours and walk-ins. Call only with consent and leave a neutral message only with separate opt-in. Preserve booking and walk-in access for patrons without a reliable phone. The paper waitlist usually has several names.
[success] At most 12 of 48 slots unused over four comparable weeks, no privacy complaints, no loss of access for patrons without a phone, and at most 10 desk minutes per weekday. Track unbooked slots, no-shows and cancellations/refills separately. Change course if reach or attendance is too low; the previous trial did not prove benefit.
known_good: The pivotal evidence is ten confirmed no-shows, eight associated with preventable reminder errors, versus just one cancellation; routine neutral consent-based reminders are the best-supported first change. A cancellation-only intervention cannot plausibly recover four slots at the observed mix, and near-closing availability explains only the unbooked category. Use the prior reminder privacy complaint and distinguish confirmations from actual attendance. Keep the 12-of-48 four-week target and preserve access, privacy and staff-time limits. Credit a different recommendation only if it explains how it can plausibly improve four slots under these facts.
decision_key: Ten confirmed no-shows (eight reminder-related) versus one cancellation, with no effective routine reminder.
